question.problem:
The scores in a standardized math test used for university admissions in a certain country are normally distributed with a mean of $57$ and a standard deviation of $16.$ Suppose $50$ test results are selected at random. What is the probability that the mean score for this sample will be less than $55?$

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-1.0\,$ | $\,0.1469\,$ | $\,0.1446\,$ | $\,0.1423\,$ | $\,0.1401\,$ | $\,0.1379\,$ |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1711\,$ | $\,0.1685\,$ | $\,0.1660\,$ | $\,0.1635\,$ | $\,0.1611\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.1977\,$ | $\,0.1949\,$ | $\,0.1922\,$ | $\,0.1894\,$ | $\,0.1867\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

 then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

We're told that the population mean $\mu =57$ the population standard deviation $\sigma =16,$ and that the sample size $n=50.$ Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(57,\frac{{16}^{2}}{50}) \\  & ∼N(57,5.12).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(\overset{―}{X}<55).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<55) & =P(Z<\frac{55-57}{\sqrt{5.12}}) \\  & ≈P(Z<-0.88) \\  & =Φ(-0.88)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(-0.88)=0.1894.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}<55) & ≈Φ(-0.88) \\  & =0.1894.\end{aligned}
$$
